content.title: What is the Streams API?
content.description: The Streams API, introduced in Java 8, provides a functional and declarative approach to processing collections of data using operations such as filtering, mapping, sorting, and reducing.

content.content: The Streams API allows developers to process data efficiently without modifying the original collection. Instead of writing multiple loops, Streams enable operations to be chained together, resulting in cleaner, more readable, and often more efficient code.

content.title: Why Use Streams?
content.content: Streams simplify collection processing, reduce boilerplate code, support functional programming, enable parallel processing, and improve code readability.
A stream processes data through a pipeline consisting of a source, one or more intermediate operations, and a terminal operation.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Streams do not store data. They simply process data from a source through a sequence of operations.

content.content: Streams can be created from collections, arrays, files, or generated dynamically using utility methods.

content.title: Creating a Stream
content.code:
List<String> names = Arrays.asList("Alice", "Bob", "Charlie");

Stream<String> stream = names.stream();

content.content: Intermediate operations transform a stream and return another stream, allowing multiple operations to be chained together.
Terminal operations complete the stream pipeline and produce a result such as a collection, value, or side effect.

rows: Perform an action on each element

left_points: Processes one element at a time

items.question: filter()
items.answer: Selects elements matching a given condition.

items.question: map()
items.answer: Transforms each element into another form.

items.question: sorted()
items.answer: Sorts stream elements naturally or using a comparator.

items.question: reduce()
items.answer: Combines all elements into a single result.

content.title: Stream Operations
content.time_complexity: Depends on the operations performed (typically O(n) for traversal)
content.space_complexity: Depends on intermediate operations and collected results

items.question: Data Filtering
items.answer: Select records based on specific conditions.

items.question: Statistics
items.answer: Calculate sums, averages, minimums, and maximums.

items.question: Parallel Processing
items.answer: Improve performance by processing large datasets concurrently.

content.title: Water Purification Pipeline
content.content: Imagine water flowing through multiple filters before reaching a storage tank. Each filter performs one operation, and the purified water represents the final result. Streams process data similarly through a sequence of operations.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Streams API, filter(), map(), reduce(), collect(), parallelStream(), Collectors, lazy evaluation, terminal operations, and method references are among the most frequently asked Java interview topics.

items.question: Can a stream be reused after a terminal operation?
items.answer: No. Once a terminal operation executes, the stream is consumed and cannot be reused.

items.question: Do streams modify the original collection?
items.answer: No. Streams process data without changing the original source unless explicitly modified.

items.question: Should parallel streams always be used?
items.answer: No. They are beneficial mainly for large datasets and CPU-intensive operations.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: A stream is a sequence of data processed through a pipeline of intermediate operations followed by a terminal operation.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: A stream consists of source, intermediate operations, and terminal operations.
Streams do not modify the original collection.
Parallel streams use multiple threads for processing.
